_comment: FICTIONAL inputs for the Milestone 5 adjustment goldens (see RULES.md). 'scenarios' are evaluateAdjustmentScenario inputs; 'historyCases' are summariseHistory inputs (record and baseline sets live in history-records.json and history-baselines.json); 'riskCases' are forecastAdjustmentRisk inputs. Expected results are in expected.json, keyed by case id, and were derived by hand/script from RULES.md and the M2 fixtures, never from engine output.
policyProfilesNote: Policy profiles map '<adjustmentType>' -> '<component>' -> handling. A missing entry means the handling is 'unconfigured'. Use them to build policyFn(type, component). Types are reweight, remeasure, combined and correction (correction has only separate_fee).

scenarios.description: E1. Weight-only correction 3.0 -> 3.4 lb on a 10x8x6 package. DIM 480/139 = 3.4532 lb bills 4 lb on both sides, so nothing moves.
E2. Weight-only increase 3 -> 5 lb on a 10x8x6 package: the corrected weight leaves the DIM-governed 4 lb bracket. Reweigh rule 3.00 only.
Same bracket: 4.2 -> 4.8 lb. Actual weight governs on both sides and both round up to 5 lb.
DIM-governed zero: 14x10x8 package, 2 lb -> 5 lb. DIM 1120/139 = 8.0576 lb bills 9 lb whatever the actual weight (up to 9 lb).
Price plateau: UPS Ground zone 2, 1 lb -> 2 lb on a 6x4x2 package. Both brackets are below the 8.50 service minimum, so the counted total is the same although billable weight changes.
Remeasure only: 3 lb, 10x8x6 -> 14x10x8. DIM 8.0576 lb bills 9 lb. Remeasure rule 4.00 only.
Remeasure where no dimensions were known: 3 lb, no dimensions -> 3 lb, 10x8x6. The declared side is an estimate.
Remeasure by 0.1 in: 15.4x10x10 -> 15.5x10x10, 3 lb. nearest_whole rounds 15.4 to 15 and 15.5 to 16; the result echoes the rounded dimensions.
Remeasure 15.4 -> 15.3 in: different input, same rounded dimensions (15), so nothing moves.

E4. Combined correction 3 lb -> 5 lb and 10x8x6 -> 14x10x8 with reweight 3.00 and remeasure 4.00 rules, no group: the difference is 2.83, not 0.56 + 2.83. Handling comes from the explicit combined policy row.
Combined correction with the reweight (priority 1) and remeasure (priority 2) rules in one exclusivity group: the engine keeps the higher priority, 4.00.
Weight-only correction 3 -> 5 lb while a grouped reweight/remeasure pair is configured: only the reweight rule is in scope, so the fee is 3.00 (not the higher-priority 4.00).
Dimension-only correction 3 lb, 10x8x6 -> 14x10x8 with the grouped pair: only the remeasure rule is in scope, fee 4.00.
Weight-only correction 3 -> 5 lb with BOTH a reweigh 3.00 and a remeasure 4.00 rule configured (no group): only 3.00 is shown (not 7.00).
Dimension-only correction 3 lb, 10x8x6 -> 14x10x8 with both rules configured: 4.00 only.
E3. Weight-only 49 -> 52 lb in a 20x20x20 box: DIM 8000/139 = 57.55 lb bills 58 lb on both sides, but Additional handling (weight > 50 lb actual) flips on.
E5. Declared 3 lb with no dimensions vs corrected 3 lb at 50x10x10: the declared side is an estimate and 20.00 of the difference rests on a charge that could not be decided on the declared side.
E5. Declared 6 lb with no dimensions vs corrected 6 lb at 50x10x10.
E7. 10 percent conditional reweight rule on the E2 shipment: the line is 10 percent of the CORRECTED base rate, 1.16.
E7. Residential 3 -> 5 lb in the 3PL default context (no customer overrides).
E7. The same shipment for the fixture customer with overrides (residential waived, fuel 10.00 percent): the customer's own difference is 0.54.
Customer exception (exclude) on the reweigh rule: the fee is waived for this customer.
Service terms bundle the reweigh rule into the rate (includedSurchargeKeys).
E8. USPS Ground Advantage 7.9 oz -> 8.1 oz (10x6x1, zone 5). No USPS adjustment-fee rule exists, so the fee is not configured.
No adjustment-fee rule exists in the context at all: UPS 3 -> 5 lb.
Only a remeasure rule exists; the correction is weight-only, so no in-scope rule exists and the fee is not configured.
A reweigh rule restricted to DAS ZIPs; the destination 85001 is not in the list: the rule exists but does not apply.
The same rule for destination 93920 (a DAS ZIP, zone 3): the fee applies. DAS 4.00 sits on both sides.
The DAS-restricted reweigh rule while no ZIP lists are loaded: the outcome is unknown.
Declared 151 lb (above the 150 lb card maximum) corrected to 140 lb.
E5. Declared 140 lb corrected to 151 lb: the corrected side is above the card maximum.
E5. 3 lb, 10x8x6 corrected to 60x40x40: DIM 96000/139 = 690.6 lb bills 691 lb, above the card maximum.
E5. UPS 2nd Day Air 30 lb corrected to 31 lb: the 2nd Day Air card ends at 30 lb.
Both sides above the card maximum: 151 lb -> 160 lb.
A correction entry with no changed field.
USPS 0.5 lb corrected to 8 oz: the same weight in another unit.
Declared weight 0 lb entered (the engine rejects weights that are not greater than zero).
declaredSource wms_fallback with a 0 lb fallback weight.
Origin ZIP with 4 digits.
Two correction entries for a one-package shipment.
Declared without dimensions, correction gives only a length.
Credit: declared 8 lb, actual 5 lb (10x8x6). The corrected charge is lower; no fee is shown.
Credit on one package of two: 5,5 lb -> 5,3 lb, residential. The sign is that of the shipment total.
E6. Three packages 3,3,3 lb, only package 1 corrected to 5 lb, one shipment-level reweigh fee.
E6. As above with a PER-PACKAGE reweigh rule: the engine emits a line for each package, only the corrected package's line is kept.
Ship date 2026-09-15: fuel v1 (14.00 percent) is in force. Residential, zone 2, 5 -> 20 lb.
Ship date 2026-09-15 on the E2 shipment (3 -> 5 lb, commercial): fuel v1 14.00 percent.
The same shipment on 2026-10-15 under fuel v2 (15.50 percent): the difference changes with the date.
Ship date 2026-12-01: fuel v2 and the peak residential surcharge (1.50 per package) are in force.
WMS fallback: the label was created at the 1 lb fallback weight with known dimensions 10x8x6; the carrier measured 5 lb.
WMS fallback: a scale failure lost both weight and dimensions (1 lb fallback, no dimensions); the carrier measured 5 lb and 10x8x6.
A reweight rule stored with charge class definite: forced to conditional, with a warning. It must not enter the counted totals.
A shipping_charge_correction rule (5.00) is kept for every adjustment type: a weight-only correction shows it, handled by the correction policy row.
Reweight 3.00 and correction 5.00 both fire on a weight correction; lines have different handling, so the component handling is mixed.
E2 shipment with postage absorbed and the fee passed through.
E2 shipment with the fee under manual approval.
E2 shipment with the fee absorbed.
E2 shipment where the fee policy row does not exist.
E2 shipment with no policy rows at all.
Remeasure scenario under the combined_explicit profile: the remeasure rows (pass_through both) decide, not the absorbed reweight rows.
Reweight scenario under the combined_explicit profile: the reweight rows are absorbed.
F2 (b). A reweigh fee rule that lists the residential surcharge as suppressed: the postage difference is still the plain +0.57 and the fee is still 3.00; only a warning is added.
F2 (c). A per-package reweigh rule in the DAS exclusivity group (priority 5), destination 93920 (a DAS ZIP), correction 3.0 -> 3.0001 lb: the billable weight does not move, so nothing is adjusted.
F2 (c). The same rule and destination with a real correction 3 -> 5 lb: the DAS surcharge stays on both sides, postage +0.42, fee 3.00 for package 0.
F2 (d). A definite peak surcharge (1.50) conditioned on the reweigh rule applying: the postage difference does not contain it.
F2 (e). A per-package reweigh rule with a 20 lb billable-weight floor, correction 3.0 -> 3.5 lb: the floor must not reach the postage.
F2 (e). The same floor rule with a real correction 3 -> 5 lb: postage +0.56, fee 3.00 for package 0.
A percent fee on 'base rate plus all surcharges': the fee pass keeps the 3PL's other surcharges as context, so the base includes the residential line (1.66, not 1.16).

F4. Two packages with a per-package reweigh rule: package 0 is corrected on paper 3.0 -> 3.4 lb but still bills 4 lb at the same price; package 1 really moves 3 -> 8 lb. Only package 1 draws the fee (3.00, not 6.00).
F4. Two packages with a per-package reweigh rule, both corrected on paper (3.0 -> 3.4 and 3.0 -> 3.3 lb), neither bills differently: no_adjustment.

F4 (decision as written: billable weight, rounded dimensions OR counted price). Package 0 is 20 lb and gets one inch taller (10x8x6 -> 10x8x7): its billable weight and price do not change, its rounded dimensions do; package 1 really moves. Both draw the per-package remeasure fee.
F5. A shipment-level 10 percent reweigh fee on two 3 lb packages, only package 1 corrected to 8 lb: the fee is 10 percent of package 1's base rate only (1.30) and the line says it covers package 1.
F5. The same fee with both packages corrected to 8 lb: each package's percent is rounded to cents and the two are added (2.60), not one rounding of the whole (2.61); the line covers packages 0 and 1.
F5. A shipment-level FLAT fee is one charge per shipment whatever the package count: its line lists no covered packages (null).
F11. no_adjustment with NO fee rule configured at all: the fee is not_triggered (design v2 3.1(6)), not not_configured.
F11. The price plateau (status ok, direction none) with NO fee rule configured: the fee is not_configured (it is not a no_adjustment case: a billable weight changed).

F2 (c). The per-package reweigh rule sits in the DAS group at the LOWEST priority: inside the group DAS would win and the fee line would be dropped. The fee must still be shown: exclusivity is kept among fee rules only.

F2. A percent fee on 'base plus all surcharges' that lists the residential surcharge in excludesRuleKeys: the list is ignored, so the base still holds the 5.00 residential line (1.66) and the postage keeps it too (+0.57).

historyCases.description: Baseline present: brand A, window January only. 12 distinct package keys over 13 rows, one same-ref pair, one row without a reference, weights-only rows, credits, a zero row, an explicit zero fee, a null fee.
Same scope, numerator filtered to type reweight: the denominator is unchanged (type filters apply to the numerator only).
Tenant-wide: only the brand-null baseline (4,000 packages) with every brand's January records, including the unmatched-brand row.
Brand B only uses brand B's own baseline.
Baseline absent: brand C has records but no baseline. Incidence is not computed; averages are still shown.
n = 0: no records and no baseline: nothing is computed.
A February window while only a January baseline exists: the baseline is not wholly inside the window, so it is not used (incidence not computed).
Two brand-A baselines whose periods overlap: the statistic is refused.
A brand-A statistic with an explicitly chosen tenant-wide baseline is refused.
A tenant-wide statistic with an explicitly chosen brand-A baseline is refused.
Two adjacent (non-overlapping) brand-A baselines are summed within the scope: N = 1000 + 1200.
k > N: five distinct packages against a baseline of 3 packages.
k = 0 with N > 0 (and n = 0 records): incidence 0.0000%, Wilson upper bound 0.7625%.
Wilson k = 3, N = 100.
Wilson k = 20, N = 1000.
k = 1, N = 3200: 0.03125 percent displays 0.0313 (HALF_UP at 4 dp).
Even count: median of 1,2,3,4 is 2.50.
Odd count: median of 1,2,3,4,10 is 3.00.
n = 29 charge records: severity confidence low.
n = 30 charge records: severity confidence adequate.
Two rows (reweight and remeasure) on one package reference count once.
Rows without a package reference count once per row (perRecordCounting).
R5: 6 charges of +10.00 and 4 credits of -5.00 in 1000 packages.
Mean exactly at a half of one E4 unit: 16 charges totalling 0.18 -> 112.5 E4 -> 113 (HALF_UP).
Fees 2.02 and 2.03: mean 2.025 exactly (20,250 E4).
Window ended 2026-09-30, today 2026-10-16 (16 days), maturityDays 30: immature.
Window ended exactly 16 days ago with maturityDays 16: mature (immature only when strictly fewer days than maturityDays).
maturityDays 17 with 16 days elapsed: immature.
Typed baseline with labels_missing_weight = 40 of 1000 packages: missingRatePct 4.0000, correctionRatePct = wms_no_weight packages / 40.
Missing and correction rates over two adjacent baselines: (40 + 30) of 2200.
labels_missing_weight = 0: missing rate 0.0000, correction rate not computed (division by zero is never 0).
Brand B baseline without labels_missing_weight: both rates are not computed.
Service filter ground while one UPS record has no resolved service: refused with the unresolved count.
Carrier and service filter usps / ground advantage: every record resolved, its own baseline (400 packages).
No carrier or service filter: the carrier-null service-null baseline (1000) and all seven records (one unresolved service is fine without a service filter).
Carrier filter ups with no service: no baseline has (ups, null), so the denominator is absent (baselines of other keys are never reused).
Type remeasure and cause carrier_remeasure on the main set: numerator filters only.
F11 / amendment A2: the same package reference 1ZSHARED on two customers is two packages (a reference alone is not unique across customers): tenant-wide k = 3 (not 2) from 4 records.
F11 / amendment A2: customer A's two records on its one package 1ZSHARED (a reweight and a remeasure) count once: k = 2 from 3 records, over customer A's own 400-package baseline.

riskCases.description: R1: V = 1000, k = 20 of N = 1000 (p = 2%), postage 10.00 and fee 5.00 per affected package, declared weights, both pass_through.
R2: as R1 on actual weights: postage is already in the forecast, only the fee is counted here.
R2: actual weights with postage ABSORBED: counted add-on 100.00 (fee), the 200.00 of in-forecast postage is reported as a staff memo with a warning.
R3: declared, postage manual_approval, fee pass_through.
R3: declared, postage manual_approval, fee unconfigured: 'So far', the identity still totals 300.00.
T1: declared_weights weights, postage pass_through, fee pass_through (fee is never in a forecast, so it is always counted here).
T1: declared_weights weights, postage manual_approval, fee pass_through (fee is never in a forecast, so it is always counted here).
T1: declared_weights weights, postage absorbed, fee pass_through (fee is never in a forecast, so it is always counted here).
T1: declared_weights weights, postage unconfigured, fee pass_through (fee is never in a forecast, so it is always counted here).
T1: actual_weights weights, postage pass_through, fee pass_through (fee is never in a forecast, so it is always counted here).
T1: actual_weights weights, postage manual_approval, fee pass_through (fee is never in a forecast, so it is always counted here).
T1: actual_weights weights, postage absorbed, fee pass_through (fee is never in a forecast, so it is always counted here).
T1: actual_weights weights, postage unconfigured, fee pass_through (fee is never in a forecast, so it is always counted here).
R4: V = 333, entered p = 1.5%, postage 0, fee 10.00: affected 4.995 (shown 5.0), total 49.95, per shipment 0.1500, annual 599.40.
R4: V = 1000, k = 1 of N = 200 (0.5%), fee severity 2.025 (mean of 2.02 and 2.03): 10.125, shown 10.13, annual 121.50 (not 121.56), per shipment 0.0101.
R4: k = 1, N = 3200 displays 0.0313% but V = 1,000,000 uses 312.5 affected exactly.

R4: V = 1000, p = 0.35% entered, severity 0.0357 on both components: each exact amount is 0.12495 -> E4 0.1250 (shown 0.13, not 0.12); counted total is the sum of the rounded components 0.2500 while the exact sum is 0.2499, so per shipment, per 1,000 and annual come from the exact sum.
R5: V = 1000, N = 1000, 6 charges of +10.00 and 4 credits of -5.00: exposure uses the 6 charges only (60.00); credits -20.00 and net 40.00 are memos.
R6: k = 0, N = 500: expected exposure 0.00, Wilson upper bound 0.7625%, high affected 7.6 at V = 1000.
k = 0 with the severities unknown: expected exposure is still 0.00 (zero incidence), the high end is null (severity unknown), confidence none.
R7: brand A at V = 1000 from its own history (k = 10, N = 1000): 10.0 affected.
R7: the same brand with the tenant-wide history (k = 280, N = 10000) chosen explicitly: 28.0 affected (2.8x), labelled by the caller as tenant-wide history.
Spec F9: V = 10,000, p = 0.5% entered, postage 2.40, fee 3.00, declared: affected 50.0, total 270.00, per shipment 0.0270, per 1,000 27.00, annual 3,240.00.
Spec F9 on actual weights: only the fee: total 150.00, per shipment 0.0150, per 1,000 15.00.
V = 0: affected 0.0, totals 0.00, per-shipment null, annual 0.00.
Entered p = 0: expected exposure 0.00.
Entered p = 100: every package is affected.
History source with no baseline (N = 0): incidence null, exposure null with a reason, never 0.00.
No baseline at all but incidence entered as 2: computed from the entered value and labelled entered.
Postage severity unknown, fee known, declared: the postage component is not_computed (listed), the total is flagged at least.
Both severities unknown: nothing is computed, total null.
Actual weights with the fee severity unknown: postage is in the forecast, the fee is not_computed, nothing counted here, total null.
Both components manual_approval: the whole 300.00 is a 0..300.00 range.
Declared: postage absorbed, fee unconfigured, so the buckets hold absorbed 200.00 and not decided 100.00.
k > N is refused.
Entered p < 0 is refused.
Entered p > 100 is refused.
Negative monthly volume is refused.
Monthly volume above 5,000,000 is refused.
Non-numeric monthly volume is refused.
The forecast basis has no default: a missing basis is refused.
A negative entered severity is refused (credits are never an input to exposure).
V x p x severity beyond the safe E4 integer range is refused (RangeError in the engine): 5,000,000 x 100% x 1,000,000.00 = 5e12 dollars = 5e16 E4 > 9.007e15.

F6: R5's history (6 charges of +10.00 and 4 credits of -5.00 in 1000 packages) on ACTUAL weights: the postage of the 6 charges is already in the user's forecast (60.00, in_forecast), the fee severity is 0, so what is counted here is 0.00; the credit memo is -20.00 but the net memo is null (a postage credit has no counterpart in a fee-only total: it used to read 0.00 - 20.00 = -20.00, a net gain).
F3: k = 0 of N = 3 with unknown severities: the Wilson lower bound is exactly 0, so the low end of the range is 0 (not null); the high end stays null (severity unknown).

F3: k = N = 6 at V = 42,946.95: the Wilson upper bound is exactly 1, so the high end of the affected range equals V (42,947.0 at one decimal, HALF_UP) and the high exposure is V x 100% x the severities.
F7: two severities whose sum exceeds the safe integer range (17,996 + 9,007,199,254,740,991 = 9,007,199,254,758,987 > 9,007,199,254,740,991) are refused with overflow, even at V = 0.
